title: Copyists today, and trumpet players imitating Louis
summary: They discuss Michael White copying Johnny Dodds, trumpeters copying Louis, and Joe's self-described poor copying.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: And maybe it was just young White kids as opposed to young Black kids. But for instance, there's a clarinet player now named Michael White in New Orleans. He's a young Black dude, about thirty maybe. And he plays like Johnny Dodds. He copies Johnny Dodds!
I wonder why people in their younger days don't seem to have the individuality, or don't seem to strive for the individuality...
Well, I don't know why. But although when you mention it... Guy Kelly wanted to play like Louis.
I know that. Because he used to play it all the time.

Then there's a funny thing again. Now, a lot of the trumpet players, practically all of them are the opposite of clarinet players. If you talk to clarinet players, they say, 'I just wanted to play like myself.' Practically all of the trumpet players, the New Orleans guys, most of them, 'Oh, I just wanted to play like Louis.' I mean, you could names all the way down the line.
I know. Louis influenced so many of those guys. One thing about me, I never had a big desire to copy. I used to admire a lot of those guys; I liked what

they played. But in the first place, I'm a very poor copier. I can't copy too much of that stuff. Because I would really sound too mechanical if I stood like guys like Ron Loinie(?), sitting right next door to... George Lewis, note for note.
i cannot do that. I couldn't sound like George Lewis if I wanted to.
And in Europe there's a million more than here.
Every little dog town has got its George Lewis and Jim Robinson and Kid Howard and that...
I know it. They want that vibrato, a lot of them don't want that vibrato like Sidney Bechet...
Do you think it's just maybe a sign of the times?
Well, or a sign of talent or something. I don't know...
